correctness.rationale: The face condition is maximum induced degree one, equivalent here to forbidding a three-vertex path as a subgraph. An independently written check (independent_check.py; preflight.txt and reproduction.txt) exhausts the 14-vertex subsets, reproduces 553 pairs and topologically sorts all 1,115 nonempty faces and 4,298 oriented Hasse incidences. The critical cells are one vertex and eight four-cells, proving the integral nonequivariant wedge by discrete Morse theory. Connectedness makes the two parts intrinsic; permutations preserving the Fano line family give the 168 part-preserving maps, and composition with the given polarity enumerates the other coset. Exhaustive signed fixed-simplex traces agree on all eight rows; the reduced degree-four sign is positive and the reduced augmentation contributes -1. The resulting character has squared sum 336 and sum zero, proving absolute irreducibility and absence of invariants. This does not assert an equivariant wedge equivalence. The frozen verifier was not executed.

value.rationale: Fano nonincidence is a canonical symmetric graph outside the standard higher-independence families. A verified integral wedge together with its full symmetry action provides a reusable test case for equivariant higher-independence topology: restriction alone would miss which full-group extension occurs and whether the full action has invariants. The precise realization and degree, not a new name for a known abstract representation, are the useful data.
